I added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`. It returns a JSON list of the logins of users created in the last 7 days, and only admins can call it. I didn't run the build or any tests, and I didn't add a test for the new endpoint.

- **Repository:** `UserRepository` has a new derived query, `findAllByCreatedDateAfter(Instant)`.
- **Service:** `UserService.getRecentlyCreatedUserLogins()` uses `Instant.now(clock).minus(7, ChronoUnit.DAYS)` and maps the matching users to their logins.
- **Endpoint:** the new method in `UserResource` is guarded with `@PreAuthorize` using `AuthoritiesConstants.ADMIN`. The mapping sits before `/users/{login}`, and Spring prefers the literal path anyway.
- **Clock:** `docs/conventions.md` requires an injected `Clock`, and the project had none. I added `config/ClockConfiguration.java` with a `Clock.systemUTC()` bean and a `Clock` parameter on the `UserService` constructor. I found no `new UserService(...)` calls under `src`, so nothing else should need changing.

I didn't update the `notes/` folder from your vault rules, because this project has no `notes/` directory yet.
